text:
A: Hiya! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah. Hi.
A: Great. I'm Kerry, I'm down in Taunton. Somerset.
B: Gareth. Basingstoke.
A: Ooh, Basingstoke. I've only ever seen it from the M3, to be honest. Is that a dog lead on your cupboard there?
B: Er, yeah. Bonnie. Labrador cross.
A: Snap, look, mine's on the back door. Moss, springer spaniel, he's ten. Went up the Quantocks on Sunday and he rolled in something absolutely disgusting, had to hose him down in the garden. Darren was not impressed.
B: Bonnie does that. Fox, usually.
A: Fox is the worst, isn't it? You can't get the smell off. So what do you do, Gareth?
B: Structural engineer. Warehouses, retail units, that sort of thing.
A: Oh, right. I'm a radiographer, so I suppose we both sort of look inside things to check they're not broken.
B: *(pause)* Yeah. Sort of, yeah.
A: Sorry, that was a terrible joke. Is that what you'd call it, checking they're not broken?
B: More checking they won't break. Before they're built.
A: Ah, see, I only get them after. People come in having fallen off a ladder, and I'm there going, right, arm up for me, my love. It's mostly general X-ray, a bit of CT. And the car park's a nightmare, that's the main thing about my job really. Twenty minutes going round some mornings.
B: Sorry, say that again? You cut out a bit.
A: The car park. Nightmare. Twenty minutes.
B: Ah. The A33's like that for me. Roadworks.
A: Do you drive in every day?
B: Three days. Home the other two. Suits me with the kids.
A: How many have you got?
B: Two. Fifteen and twelve. Callum and Ellie.
A: Oh, lovely. Busy, then.
B: Yeah. I forgot it was non-uniform day last week. Ellie went in in her uniform and everyone else was in their own clothes.
A: Oh no! *(laughs)* Was she furious?
B: Pretty furious, yeah. I'm on my own with them most of the week, so it's sort of on me now.
A: Well, honestly, I'd forget too. That's why I have the calendar on the wall there, everything goes on it, all my shifts, Darren's jobs, the dog's jabs. And I do a spreadsheet for the camping. We go to Bude every summer with friends and I do the packing list for everyone. They take the mick, but nobody's ever forgotten a tent peg.
B: I took the kids to a caravan in Devon once. I forgot the bedding.
A: All the bedding?
B: All of it.
A: *(laughs)* Oh, Gareth. You need me. Did you at least have a cream tea while you were down there?
B: Yeah, think so.
A: Jam first or cream first?
B: Er. Didn't really think about it.
A: Well, you're in Devon, they'd have done cream first, which is wrong. Jam first, always. I'll die on that hill.
B: Fair enough. I just eat it.
A: That's the most dangerous answer you could've given. Sorry, am I going on? Do you get to watch much football with all that?
B: Saints, yeah. On the telly mostly. I go a couple of times a—
